headline: Records keep climbing on narrow AI leadership ahead of Fed minutes
body: Equities notched fresh records again this week, with the S&P 500 closing above 7,800 for the first time and the Nasdaq Composite also printing an all-time high, helped by Treasury yields easing and crude oil slipping. The advance stayed narrowly led: Nvidia and AMD both touched new highs, with AMD popping roughly 2.8% after CEO Lisa Su flagged a ramp in chip supply for next year, while market breadth has thinned to the point where only around a quarter of S&P 500 constituents trade above their own 50-day moving averages. That combination -- index-level records built on a shrinking slice of outperformers -- is the kind of setup that tends to keep momentum traders engaged while raising the bar for what a genuine broadening of the rally would require.

Today's macro focus centers on the Fed and whether the tape is more than a single-sector story. Minutes from last month's FOMC meeting are due this afternoon, with several regional Fed presidents also on the speaking calendar, giving the market fresh language to parse on the path for rates. Gold's continued push toward record territory alongside record equities suggests some investors are still hedging policy uncertainty even as they stay long risk assets, a mild tension underneath an otherwise constructive tape. Retail-specific chatter did not surface anything distinct enough to flag today, so this read leans primarily on price action, sector leadership, and the macro calendar rather than social sentiment.
